## Purpose

Regional marker-gene expression mapped in space — Figure 4A. Reads the frozen 8 µm object
and writes one spatial map per gene per sample.

## Outputs

Hi-res spatial expression maps of four regional marker genes — **Fabp1, Reg1** (proximal /
duodenum) and **Fabp6, Slc10a2** (distal / ileum, bile-acid transport) — across the four
Visium HD samples. Everything is written to `../outputs/`.

**Manuscript panel (Figure 4A)**

The published panel shows exactly **one Duodenum image and one Ileum image per gene** —
8 images total, not all four sample replicates.

| Output | Gene | Region |
|---|---|---|
| `fig4A_spatial_Fabp1_Duodenum_3_008um.pdf` | Fabp1 | Duodenum |
| `fig4A_spatial_Fabp1_Ileum_3_008um.pdf` | Fabp1 | Ileum |
| `fig4A_spatial_Reg1_*` | Reg1 | both |
| `fig4A_spatial_Fabp6_*` | Fabp6 | both |
| `fig4A_spatial_Slc10a2_*` | Slc10a2 | both |

**Published replicate.** Every representative spatial panel in this manuscript uses
Duodenum_3 and Ileum_3. Duodenum_4 and Ileum_2 are the second biological replicate — real
data, but not printed — so their outputs carry the `supporting_` prefix rather than
`fig4A_`.
>
> Note for the eventual GEO submission: at deposition time these samples are renamed
> `Duodenum_3` → `Duodenum_1`, `Ileum_3` → `Ileum_1` (and `Duodenum_4` → `Duodenum_2`,
> `Ileum_2` stays `Ileum_2`). Not applied to any code or filename yet — GEO naming and
> internal project naming are deliberately kept separate until submission.

**Supporting — not in the published figure**

| Output | What it is |
|---|---|
| `supporting_spatial_<gene>_all_samples.pdf` | all four samples for that gene on one row, for side-by-side QC comparison |
| `supporting_spatial_<gene>_Duodenum_4_008um.pdf` | the other Duodenum replicate — real data, not the printed panel |
| `supporting_spatial_<gene>_Ileum_2_008um.pdf` | the other Ileum replicate — real data, not the printed panel |

These four files were previously named `fig4b_spatial_<gene>_all_samples.pdf` and sat
alongside the panel outputs with no visual distinction. They are QC composites, not
panel sources — the published figure never shows all four samples together.

**Filename note.** This notebook and its outputs were previously named `Fig4B_*` /
`fig4b_*`. That was wrong: this is manuscript panel **4A**. Figure 4B is RNAscope
imaging and has no code — see the manuscript figure legends.

# Setup

```{r config}
rds_hires <- "../data/final_analysis_object_with_master_deconv_hires.RDS"
out_dir   <- "../outputs"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

op   <- function(f) file.path(out_dir, f)     # path helper for outputs
ubar <- function(x) gsub("\\.", "_", x)       # "Ileum.2.008um" -> "Ileum_2_008um"

FIG4A_GENES <- c("Fabp1", "Reg1", "Fabp6", "Slc10a2")
```

```{r load}
merged.object <- readRDS(rds_hires)
sample_images <- Images(merged.object)

genes_present <- intersect(FIG4A_GENES, rownames(merged.object))
missing <- setdiff(FIG4A_GENES, genes_present)
if (length(missing) > 0) warning("Genes not in data: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
cat("Genes plotted:", paste(genes_present, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# PART 1 — Manuscript panel

## Fig 4A — spatial expression per gene, per sample

One panel per sample per gene. The colour scale is fixed per gene across all four
samples (computed from the full range in the data), so the duodenum and ileum images
for a given gene are directly comparable.

Only Duodenum_3 and Ileum_3 are the published replicate (confirmed by the author,
project-wide — see the note above); Duodenum_4 and Ileum_2 are real data but not the
printed panel, so they're written under `supporting_` instead of `fig4A_`.

```{r panel_4a_plots, fig.width=6, fig.height=6}
PUBLISHED_REPLICATE <- c("Duodenum.3.008um", "Ileum.3.008um")

for (gene in genes_present) {
  gene_range <- range(FetchData(merged.object, vars = gene)[[gene]], na.rm = TRUE)

  plots <- lapply(sample_images, function(img) {
    p <- SpatialFeaturePlot(merged.object, features = gene, images = img,
                            pt.size.factor = 1.25, crop = TRUE)
    p[[1]] +
      scale_fill_gradientn(colours = rev(brewer.pal(11, "Spectral")),
                           limits = gene_range, name = "Expr") +
      labs(title = paste0(gene, " — ", img)) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
            legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"))
  })
  names(plots) <- sample_images

  for (img in sample_images) {
    prefix <- if (img %in% PUBLISHED_REPLICATE) "fig4A_spatial_" else "supporting_spatial_"
    ggsave(op(paste0(prefix, gene, "_", ubar(img), ".pdf")),
           plots[[img]], width = 6, height = 6)
  }
  cat("Saved 4A panels:", gene, "\n")
}
```

# PART 2 — Supporting figures

Not part of Figure 4A. Kept because side-by-side comparison of all four samples is
useful for review, even though the published panel only shows one representative per
region.

## All four samples, one row per gene

```{r supporting_all_samples, fig.width=22, fig.height=6}
for (gene in genes_present) {
  gene_range <- range(FetchData(merged.object, vars = gene)[[gene]], na.rm = TRUE)

  plots <- lapply(sample_images, function(img) {
    p <- SpatialFeaturePlot(merged.object, features = gene, images = img,
                            pt.size.factor = 1.25, crop = TRUE)
    p[[1]] +
      scale_fill_gradientn(colours = rev(brewer.pal(11, "Spectral")),
                           limits = gene_range, name = "Expr") +
      labs(title = paste0(gene, " — ", img)) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
            legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"))
  })

  p_row <- wrap_plots(plots, nrow = 1, guides = "collect")
  ggsave(op(paste0("supporting_spatial_", gene, "_all_samples.pdf")), p_row, width = 22, height = 6)
  cat("Saved supporting row:", gene, "\n")
}
```
